beta_new: Reach a flake via a shallow corner, then step rightward onto it and layback its left-facing edge to a notch, which you surmount. From there either work up a tricky slab left to a two-bolt anchor, or follow the slab and arete straight up to a higher anchor. Most parties stop after this pitch and rappel.

Either squirm up the slot behind the boulder at the base or, preferably, come across from the leftward side to the large dihedral that faces right. The corner ends at a roof; lieback rightward over it to a ledge, then step down to the belay at two bolts.

Pitch two follows a short thin crack leftward and easier rock; pitch three swings rightward to a corner before heading left to the top.
A short, steep pitch up a wall of sandy pockets that ends at a two-bolt station; a few pitons are already in place along the way.
Tucked immediately behind a cluster of large firs, the route is a slim finger-width fissure.
Clip three bolts, then bend up-left into the slender crack of the adjacent route and lower from its anchor.
Reach the foot of a hanging dihedral by climbing the face diagonally leftward; the 5.9 moves here feel scary. Then climb the corner to two bolts. This opening pitch doubles as a separate route.
Eight bolts lead directly along the rounded arete to the ledge above; watch for slightly flaky rock in the upper part.

Pitch one crosses an easy slab with no protection to a slender, curving crack, which you follow rightward before crossing beneath the arch toward a belay stance. The second pitch hand-traverses and face climbs along the arch, with a single 5.11a spot, to easier ground.

Share the opening 50 feet of the neighbouring route, then leave it once you reach the alcove, heading left into a corner that faces right. Ascend until the roof blocks you and go around its left end with a bolt for protection, then finish up the slab, clipping a pair of additional bolts, to the anchor.
A wandering slab where every difficult section is well protected. To tame rope drag, put a long sling on the traverse bolt found about midway through the first pitch.
Climb the obvious open corner and get past the roof by its right-hand end, ending at the neighbouring route's anchors. A small rack complements the few bolts present.
Seven bolts lead straight upward to a permanent anchor that sits a bit right of the neighbouring route.
Hard slab moves right off the ground, protected by four bolts, lead to an easy crack with a stance for belaying. From there, cracks continue to the top of the formation.

Begin by climbing a neighbouring route, then hand-traverse rightward to an alcove where nuts and a piton are fixed. Above, lieback two overhanging cracks beside a fixed blade; that stretch is the 11b crux.

Next comes a lieback and finger crack curving out left. Some 25 feet along it becomes an undercling at 11a, then a brief 5.9 corner ends at a stance under two corners facing left.

The first pitch opens with a boulder problem on polished holds past two bolts, the route's crux. After that, work a clumsy hand-sized crack up to a belay perch called The Bar, with a lot of air beneath it.
The first pitch follows excellent stone on the arete's right-hand side, with five bolts and the hardest moves saved for the upper part.

Begin low on the ramp, beneath the big offwidth. Jam up the left side of the small pillar called the Rat's Tooth and squeeze to a piton, then step out leftward onto a flake for the belay. The next pitch wrestles through a slot of ten inches, then undercuts leftward to a stance.

Further body-jamming, easier at 5.10a, reaches a gentle ramp, and the top is easy in either direction.

moves.from: Carry big-bro or tubular chocks along with a light rack topping out at a #4 Camalot.

value.text: Big-bro or tube chocks, plus a light rack of cams to #4.

beta_new: Climb the steep slab to the right of a neighbouring route, face-climbing through thin, fractured crack systems and clipping three bolts.

moves.from: Rappel from the anchors to the right.

beta_new: Follow the huge dihedral that leans and arches leftward on the southern wall's right-hand edge.

moves.from: The crack calls for gear as big as six inches.

beta_new: Jam the slender crack that lies between two adjacent routes. Protection is minimal: a single bolt and an epoxied placement.
Edge up the outside of the arch along a line of seven bolts to the arch belay. The route wanders over steep wall to the arch's right.

Get to the rappel stance via one of the three routes immediately beside it. Beyond the anchor, trend rightward at 11d to a sling belay where the roof ends, then climb a trough at 11a to a comfortable ledge.

Raise your belay leftward beyond a big tree (now fallen), and finish up the face above at 11a to the wall's top. Protection on these upper pitches is poor.

Pitch one follows a pale, steep dihedral under a prominent corner, laybacking and jamming a thin crack of finger and hand size, with 5.9+ moves close to the top, to a big ledge with anchors.

Rappel there, or do the shorter second pitch, which swings left beneath the steep headwall before returning right above it.

moves.from: Take a rack of cams and bigger nuts.

value.text: A rack of cams and bigger nuts.

beta_new: Open by laybacking or jamming a crack set in a corner. Next, stem and layback the corner as it sweeps leftward up to a roof, and finish with a crack above it that leads to a two-bolt anchor.

Launch from the lowest slab, close to the rock's centre, angling rightward past one bolt to a roomy ledge. The next lead begins with a brief crack beside the belay, then a lovely slab with four bolts, a small roof, and another bolt, and a two-bolt stance to finish the lead.

Above, go straight to a bolt and trace the rosy dike that bends across the slab to a little ledge. A short pitch gains a big shelf with a juniper, and a final slab with two bolts and a trough leads close to the summit, where a scramble finishes it.
Follow the good crack in the stepped corner that faces left over roughly 90 feet, then make a tricky traverse rightward to join a neighbouring route.

moves.from: Carry cams to #2 plus extra stoppers.

beta_new:
Pitch one scales the buttress on a chain of flakes, with a committing move onto a jug, then trends up-left to a diagonal-crack belay. Pitch two works across to a bolt on a neighbouring route, then up-right to a big boulder-strewn ledge.

Pitch three begins on a different route but follows a crack leftward and round into a dihedral, then a fist crack of about 15 feet joins another route for the run to the summit.

Three pitches. Start with a short, easy lead beside a flake up to a little pine for the belay. The bolted second pitch trends rightward to a band of quartz, then continues up steep face moves (roughly 5.10+) before bolts mark a belay on a gentler slab.

Finish by surmounting the arch overhead, around 5.8, then belay among the water-carved pockets known as tinajas.
Clip the line of bolts up and out through the overhang, then settle into the technical face moves above.

Roughly twenty feet off the ground a tricky lieback gives entry to a brief hand crack and then the main dihedral. Stem, bridge and rely on footwork up the dihedral, with decent gear along the way, until a step left onto an airy foothold.

Finish by squirming up a hand-crack slot, and watch for loose blocks lying on top.

Use the opening pitch of C'est la Vie, carry on through its crux, then swing out over the badly overhanging upper wall clipping 4 bolts. Pull over the lip of the roof and belay from 3 bolts just above.
Start by scaling a ramp, then shuffle left to the foot of the dihedral. Climb the dihedral itself and go over the roof capping it, where the crux comes.
Jam the slanting finger crack immediately east of the Green line all the way up; an old bolt sits at the top.
The first lead is excellent face work using flakes and small edges, finishing at a semi-hanging stance. The second heads directly up steep, rough stone to a two-bolt belay.
The first pitch climbs vertical rock rightward out of the gully with little gear, reaching a small stance. The second pitch follows an easy crack to the slabs near the summit.

moves.from: Bring RPs, wired nuts and TCUs for the protection

beta_new:
The first pitch goes via flakes beneath a corner, then a second brief corner past a bolt. Move left to a sloping stance, then smear leftward below a little roof, then go right to a shallow corner and a two-bolt shelf.

The second pitch layback leftward beside fixed pins with a committing mantle up to a narrow ledge, with easier terrain leading above.

Start roughly thirty feet along the ramp and clip eleven bolts on the black wall to a narrow ledge. Next, trace a dihedral system rightward until it fades, crank to the arete, and follow a sharply rising ramp to a belay.

The third pitch climbs a black ramp, works left under a roof, then goes straight to a ledge with an anchor.
Follow the shallow corner up the far right of the face; the lone bolt is about midway up.
Find the prominent dihedral and climb it. Continually awkward, the route is said to be cruxed by a mantel up high in the dihedral, where the gear is scary.

The first pitch is the easy opening lead of the neighbouring dihedral route, up to a belay. The second jams cracks that widen from fingers to hands, just left of a dark streak, ending at a stance under a small tree.

On the last pitch, angle rightward and upward below a little roof, pull around it on its left, and continue over easier broken ground.

moves.from: Retreat is by rappel with two ropes.
